title: A PuLP model end to end with CBC

questions.stem: A PuLP model maximizes savings. To cap crew-hours at 200, a teammate writes `prob += lpSum(h[i] * y[i] for i in S), "crew"` and forgets the `<= 200`. What does PuLP do with the line?

options.text: It adds a row named crew with no bound, which CBC reads as at most 0
options.says: An expression handed to += is not a row at all: PuLP makes it the objective.

options.text: It makes the crew-hours sum the objective, in place of the savings
options.says: Right: += with an expression sets the objective, so a row that lost its comparison replaces the objective.

options.text: It raises an error, because every row needs a comparison sign
options.says: PuLP accepts the line without an error; the lesson says the row quietly becomes the new objective.

options.text: It ignores the line, because an expression alone adds nothing
options.says: The line is not ignored: an expression given to += becomes the objective.

origin.section: A PuLP Model Is a Problem, Its Variables, and Rows Added With `+=`

questions.stem: A nightly PuLP 3.3 run with `timeLimit=600` ends with `prob.status == 1` and `prob.sol_status == 2`, and the plan is worth $41,200k. What may the nightly report say about that plan?

options.text: It is optimal, since a status of 1 always means Optimal
options.says: Status 1 also comes back when a limit stopped the search with a plan in hand; only sol_status 1 means proved.

options.text: There is none, since a sol_status of 2 means no solution
options.says: sol_status 2 is 'Solution Found': a plan exists; it is the proof of optimality that is missing.

options.text: It keeps every row, but nothing proves it is the best
options.says: Right: status 1 with sol_status 2 is a feasible plan from a search stopped early, as the one-node and time-limit runs showed.

options.text: It may break some rows, since the search stopped early
options.says: A plan with sol_status 2 keeps every row; what a stopped search lacks is the proof that no better plan exists.

origin.section: The Status Says How CBC Stopped; `sol_status` Says Whether the Plan Is Proved

questions.stem: A PuLP port and its MathOpt original of a 60-project model both report an optimal plan at their default gaps, worth $18,410k and $18,402k. What should the port test do first?

options.text: Solve both again at a gap of 0, then compare the two values
options.says: Right: at a default gap a solver may stop within its tolerance of the best, so the values are compared at gap 0.

options.text: Fail the port, since an $8k gap between them means the port lost a row
options.says: A difference within the solvers' gap tolerance proves nothing either way; the test first removes the gap.

options.text: Compare the two plans project by project, leaving the gaps as they are
options.says: Optimal plans can differ when several tie, so plans are not compared directly; each is checked against the other's rules.

options.text: Pass the port, since $8k lies within both solvers' default gaps
options.says: Being within the gap says nothing about the rows: a port that dropped a row can reach a higher value and still report optimal.

origin.section: A Port Is Proved by a Test: Same Optimum, Same Rows, Each Plan Allowed
